Sam B.: Heads up — legal flagged a community model we were about to onboard. clause looks like 'no resale' + telemetry opt-in. anyone seen this pattern before?
LicenseBot: Automated scan: model 'orchid-lite-v2' -> license: Community-NonCommercial-1.0 (restrictive). potential issue for hosting.
Maria G.: can you paste the exact clause? sometimes 'no resale' still allows hosting if we don't redistribute weights.
Sam B.: sure — 
Sam B.: ```
You may not redistribute model weights or otherwise make the Model available for direct sale or for use in a product that generates revenue, except as allowed by a separate license agreement. Telemetry: You must collect and share anonymized usage telemetry with the model author upon request.
```
Legal: quick read — the 'redistribute' + 'direct sale' sentence is broad. This blocks Hosted API by default. Dedicated/Private might be doable if customer holds the weights and we operate only as orchestration (but still risky). Telemetry clause is also a compliance hole.
Kevin L.: quantization question — if we produce a quantized/ptq variant for inference, is that considered redistribution/derivative?
Legal: in many precedents, transforming weights (quantize, prune) is still a derivative. Unless license explicitly permits derivatives, we can't ship derived weights. So we can't provide pre-quantized weights to customers under Hosted.
Tanya R.: ok action items: 1) mark Hosted=false for orchid-lite-v2 intake; 2) Dedicated=needs legal-signed addendum; 3) Private=allowed w/ customer-managed weights + KMS; 4) disable auto-telemetry toggle; 5) add eval to check quantized performance if customer supplies weights.
Sam B.: creating intake ticket now and tagging legal + eng. I'll add a short eval plan for Maria/Kevin to run when we have customer-supplied weights.
Maria G.: I'll run a quick baseline vs int8 locally on a small eval set (100 prompts) and post delta numbers. starting in ~30m.
Kevin L.: also proposing a console UX change: surface license flags and 'derivative_allowed' boolean on model detail page so SRE/solutions teams know at glance. I'll file a ticket.
Legal: thanks — please cc contracts if customer asks for an exception. if they want hosted access we'll need a separate license that explicitly grants redistribution/derivative rights.
Sam B.: noted. :thumbsup: filing ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/INF-4821 (putting notes + license excerpt).
Maria G.: quick update (after 45m): int8 drop ~1.8% on rouge-L on our sample, latency down ~2.5x. sharing full numbers in the ticket.
Tanya R.: great — let's add 'quant-eval' checklist step: sample size, metrics (ROUGE/BLEU/LL), and acceptable thresholds.
Sam B.: agreed. leaving thread open for any legal edgecases. thanks everyone. :party:
